fingerprints.story: The storm had been raging for three days, a relentless assault of salt and fury that battered the granite spine of the Blackwood Point Lighthouse. Inside the lantern room, Elias Thorne sat hunched over his workbench, the rhythmic *tick-tock* of the great Fresnel lens rotating above him serving as the only counterpoint to the howling wind outside. Elias was a man carved from the same stone as his tower—weathered, silent, and enduring.
